words.tr:
v. 停止；阻止；
n. 停止；阻止；车站；停留；
words.ex: He stopped walking when he saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到狗时，他停止了走路。
words.en: If you stop something from happening, you prevent it from happening or prevent it from continuing.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: He decided to quit smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年决定戒烟。
words.en: If you quit, or quit something, you stop doing it or leave it.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet can prevent head injuries.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔可以防止头部受伤。
words.en: To prevent something means to stop it from happening or to stop someone from doing something.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.tr:
v. 逃避；逃走；
n. 逃脱；逃避；
words.ex: He tried to escape from the prison.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃离监狱。
words.en: To escape means to get away from a place or a situation that you are in, especially because it is difficult or dangerous to stay there.

words.tr: adj. 可避免的；能防止的
words.ex: The accident was evitable if he had slowed down.
words.ex_cn: 如果他减速了，这场事故本可以避免的。
words.en: Capable of being avoided or prevented.

words.ex: Don't discourage him from trying.
words.ex_cn: 不要阻止他尝试。
words.en: If someone or something discourages you, they cause you to lose your enthusiasm about your actions.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.ex: The medicine helps reduce inhibition of the immune system.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制免疫系统的抑制。
words.en: Inhibition is a feeling that makes one self-conscious and unable to act in a relaxed and natural way.

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.tr: phrase. 保护…免受…；防护；使不受伤害
words.ex: Wear a hat to protect from the sun.
words.ex_cn: 戴帽子以防晒。
words.en: To keep safe from harm, danger, or injury.

words.tr: phrase. 使免受……的伤害；保护……不受……
words.ex: We must keep safe from the rain.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须避开雨，保证安全。
words.en: To protect or guard from harm, danger, or damage.

words.tr: phrase. 阻止；抑制；使退缩；隐瞒
words.ex: He tried to hold back his tears.
words.ex_cn: 他试图忍住眼泪。
words.en: To hold back means to prevent someone or something from moving forward or making progress, or to keep something secret or not express your feelings.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.ex: The old factory is now a derelict building.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂现在是一座破败的建筑。
words.en: If a building or a piece of land is derelict, it is not cared for and is in bad condition. A derelict person or thing is one that has been abandoned or neglected.

words.ex: He gave up smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年戒烟了。
words.en: If you give up something, you stop doing it or having it.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.tr:
n. 限制；
v. 限制；
words.ex: The teacher set a limit on homework time.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业时间设定了限制。
words.en: A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.ex: There is a restriction on smoking in this building.
words.ex_cn: 这栋楼里禁止吸烟。
words.en: A restriction is an official rule that limits what you can do or that limits the amount or size of something.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；持有；容纳；保留；举行；
n. 拿；控制；持；
words.ex: He held the rope tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; to maintain in a grasp; to keep in a specified state, relation, or position; to contain or be capable of containing; to have in one's possession; to keep back from action; to delay the action or effect of; to keep in custody; to bear, sustain, or support; to have or maintain in the mind; to consider or esteem; to assert or affirm; to organize and carry on; to have the ownership or use of; to keep from falling or moving; to remain unbroken or unyielding; to remain attached or faithful; to remain valid or effective.

words.tr:
adv. 只；仅仅；只有；
adj. 唯一的；仅有的；
words.ex: He eats only apples for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐只吃苹果。
words.en: You use only to indicate the one thing that is true, appropriate, or important in a particular situation, in contrast to all the other things that are not true, appropriate, or important.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He showed great concentration while solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解这道数学题时非常专注。
words.en: Concentration is the ability to focus all your attention on one thing without being distracted.

words.ex: Please pay attention to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 请专心听老师讲课。
words.en: To focus one's mind or efforts on something or someone, especially in order to understand or learn.

words.tr:
v. 集中；聚焦；
n. 中心点；焦点；
words.ex: He needs to focus on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

words.ex: The teacher put emphasis on reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调每天都要阅读。
words.en: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

words.ex: He specialises in repairing old clocks.
words.ex_cn: 他专用于修理老式钟表。
words.en: To concentrate on and become expert in a particular subject or skill.

words.ex: People gather in the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们在广场上聚集庆祝节日。
words.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: You must concentrate on your homework.
words.ex_cn: 你必须集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you concentrate on something, you give it your full attention and think about it carefully.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.tr: adj. 有限的； v. 限制；“limit”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: We have limited time to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 我们完成这个项目的时间是有限的。
words.en: If something is limited, there is only a certain amount of it.

words.ex: The universe may be infinite.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙可能是无限的。
words.en: If you describe something as infinite, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in amount or degree.

words.ex: He is a so-called expert, but he knows little.
words.ex_cn: 他是个所谓的专家，但懂得很少。
words.en: used to show that something or someone is commonly designated by the name or term specified, often to suggest that the name or term is not appropriate or accurate

words.ex: He is known as a good teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他被称为一位好老师。
words.en: If someone or something is known as a particular name, they are called by that name.

words.tr: v. 叫；打电话；“call”的过去式； adj. 被叫做；
words.ex: They called him Jack.
words.ex_cn: 他们叫他杰克。
words.en: To give someone or something a particular name or title; to telephone someone; to shout or summon someone.

words.tr: v. 命名；取名；“name”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 指定的；
words.ex: They named the baby Lily.
words.ex_cn: 他们给婴儿取名为莉莉。
words.en: Given a specified name or title.

words.ex: They regard him as a hero.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他视为英雄。
words.en: To consider or think of someone or something in a specified way.

words.ex: The book has a long title.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一个很长的标题。
words.en: A title is a name that describes someone's position or job, or a word or phrase that is used to describe a book, film, play, etc.

words.tr:
n. 术语；学期；期限；措辞；
v. 把…称作；把…叫做；
words.ex: The word 'algorithm' is a technical term in computer science.
words.ex_cn: ‘算法’是计算机科学中的一个术语。
words.en: A term is a word or expression used in relation to a particular subject, especially one that has a specific meaning, or a fixed period of time during which something lasts or is intended to happen.

words.ex: The dictionary gives a clear definition of the word.
words.ex_cn: 词典给出了这个词的清晰定义。
words.en: A statement of the exact meaning of a word, phrase, or concept.

words.ex: He is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的歌手。
words.en: Known about by many people.

words.tr: adj. 众所周知的；著名的
words.ex: He is a well-known singer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的歌手。
words.en: A well-known person, place, or thing is one that is known about by a lot of people.

words.ex: I am familiar with this song.
words.ex_cn: 我熟悉这首歌。
words.en: If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.ex: The concept of freedom is important in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 自由这个观念在许多国家都很重要。
words.en: A concept is an idea or abstract principle.

words.ex: He had a good idea to fix the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他想到了一个修自行车的好主意。
words.en: An idea is a thought, plan, or suggestion about what to do, or a belief or opinion.

words.ex: He has a clear notion of right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他对对错有清晰的概念。
words.en: A notion is an idea or belief about something.

words.ex: The painting gave me inspiration.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画给了我灵感。
words.en: Inspiration is a feeling of enthusiasm you get from someone or something, which gives you new and creative ideas.

words.ex: He asked for a quotation for the new computer.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了新电脑的报价。
words.en: A quotation is a sentence or phrase taken from a book, poem, play, etc., which is repeated by someone else, or a statement of the current price of something.

words.tr:
v. 引用；报价；
n. 引用；引文；报价；
words.ex: He quoted Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中引用了莎士比亚的话。
words.en: To repeat or copy out (a group of words from a text or speech), typically with an indication that one is not the original author or speaker.

words.tr:
v. 评论；表达意见；
n. 评论；意见；
words.ex: He commented on the movie last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚对这部电影发表了评论。
words.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it.

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: He is interested in linguistic patterns in children.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿童的语言模式感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to language or linguistics.

words.ex: He speaks English as his first language.
words.ex_cn: 他说英语作为他的第一语言。
words.en: Language is the system of communication in speech and writing that is used by people of a particular country or area.

words.tr:
n. 词；单词；话语；
v. 用词语表达；
words.ex: This word means 'happy' in English.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在英语中意思是‘高兴’。
words.en: A single unit of language that has meaning and can be spoken or written.

words.ex: He loves reading English literature.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢阅读英语文学。
words.en: Literature consists of written works, especially those considered to have artistic or intellectual value.

words.ex: Children need literacy to read books and write letters.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们需要有读写能力才能读书和写信。
words.en: Literacy is the ability to read and write.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.ex: He values education very much.
words.ex_cn: 他非常重视教育。
words.en: Education is the process of teaching and learning, especially in a school or college, or the knowledge that you get from this.

words.ex: My brother goes to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟每天早上上学。
words.en: A school is an institution where children are educated.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: Good communication helps people understand each other.
words.ex_cn: 良好的交流有助于人们相互理解。
words.en: The imparting or exchanging of information by speaking, writing, or using some other medium.

words.tr:
v. 交谈；说话；
n. 谈话；
words.ex: They talk every evening after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天晚饭后都会交谈。
words.en: To speak in order to give information or express ideas or feelings; conversation or discussion.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.ex: He gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个口头警告，而不是书面的。
words.en: Relating to or in the form of words.

words.ex: He speaks English every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天讲英语。
words.en: To say words in order to express thoughts, feelings, or opinions.

words.ex: He gave an oral report in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上做了口头报告。
words.en: Relating to the mouth; spoken rather than written.

words.tr: v. 叙述；给（电视或电影）作旁白
words.ex: He will narrate the story to his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他将为他的小妹妹讲述这个故事。
words.en: If you narrate a story, you tell it from your own point of view.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.ex: The signal transmission is clear and strong.
words.ex_cn: 信号传输清晰而强劲。
words.en: The act or process of sending or passing something from one place, person, or thing to another.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.tr:
n. 旅游；旅行；
v. 旅游；旅行；
words.ex: His travel to Japan was unforgettable.
words.ex_cn: 他去日本的旅游令人难忘。
words.en: If you travel, you go from one place to another, often to a place that is far away.

words.ex: They went on a long journey by train.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘火车进行了一次长途旅行。
words.en: A journey is the act of traveling from one place to another, especially when this involves a long distance or a lot of time.

words.tr:
n. 旅行；旅程；
v. 绊倒；
words.ex: We went on a trip to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山里旅行了。
words.en: A trip is a journey in which you go somewhere, usually for a short time, and come back again.

words.tr: n. 航班；飞行；（阶梯的）一段；
words.ex: The flight to Beijing leaves at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 飞往北京的航班早上8点起飞。
words.en: A flight is a journey made by flying, usually in an aircraft.

words.tr: n. 旅游；游览；巡回活动；
words.ex: We went on a tour of Paris last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天我们去巴黎旅游了。
words.en: A tour is a journey in which you visit several places that interest you, especially on holiday.

words.ex: They went on a long voyage across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了一次横跨海洋的长途航行。
words.en: A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.tr:
v. 移动；搬家；
n. 行动；移动；
words.ex: Please move the chair.
words.ex_cn: 请移动椅子。
words.en: To change position or to cause something or someone to change position, especially in a particular direction or to a particular place.

words.ex: He carries a bag to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天带一个包去学校。
words.en: To carry something means to move it while supporting it, especially in your hands or arms.

words.ex: He brings his lunch to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天带午饭去上班。
words.en: To bring something means to carry or convey it to the place where you are or to the place you are talking about.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
words.en: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

words.ex: After the break, we will proceed with the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 休息后，我们将继续开会。
words.en: If you proceed to do something, you continue to do it or start to do it after doing something else first.

words.tr: v. 兑现；递送；交付；发表；为…接生；
words.ex: He promised to deliver on his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺要兑现自己的目标。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.tr:
v. 通过；传递；路过；(时间)流逝；
n. 通行证；(考试)及格；
words.ex: He passed the exam with a high score.
words.ex_cn: 他以高分通过了考试。
words.en: To move or go past someone or something; to transfer or hand over something to someone.

words.ex: I send a message to my friend.
words.ex_cn: 我给朋友发送一条消息。
words.en: To cause to go or be taken to a particular destination; dispatch.

words.ex: The transit of goods takes three days.
words.ex_cn: 货物的运输需要三天。
words.en: The act or process of passing through or across; the conveyance of people or goods from one place to another.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: The delivery of the package took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这个包裹的交付花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of delivering letters, parcels, or goods.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 流动；
words.ex: The flow of water in the river is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 河里水的流动非常快。
words.en: To move along or out steadily and continuously in a current or stream.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.ex: Birds begin migration in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在秋天开始迁徙。
words.en: The movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, especially regularly according to the seasons.

words.ex: Immigration to this country has increased recently.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的移民数量最近增加了。
words.en: Immigration is the act of coming to live permanently in a country that is not your own.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.tr: n. 车辆；交通工具；媒介；
words.ex: The vehicle stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在红灯前停了下来。
words.en: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people or goods from place to place.

words.ex: He drives a red car to work.
words.ex_cn: 他开车去上班。
words.en: A car is a motor vehicle with four wheels, usually propelled by an internal combustion engine.

words.tr: n. 马达；发动机；机动车；
words.ex: The car has a strong motor.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有一个强大的马达。
words.en: A motor is a device that changes energy into mechanical motion, especially such a device that provides power for a vehicle or for another device with moving parts.

words.ex: The traffic on the highway was very heavy this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上高速公路上的交通非常拥堵。
words.en: Traffic refers to the movement of vehicles or people along roads, or to the movement of aircraft, ships, or trains. It can also refer to the trade or exchange of goods or services, especially illegal ones.

words.tr:
n. 输出；出口；
v. 输出；出口；
words.ex: This country is a big export of wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家是小麦的大输出国。
words.en: To send goods to another country for sale.

words.tr:
n. 进口；重要性；
v. 进口；
words.ex: The country increased its import of oil last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家增加了石油的进口。
words.en: To bring in (goods or services) from a foreign country for sale or use.

words.tr: phrase. 开始从事；喜欢；形成...的习惯
words.ex: He took to swimming every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他开始每天早上游泳来保持健康。
words.en: To begin to like someone or something; to start doing something as a habit or regular activity.

words.ex: He will introduce his friend to the class.
words.ex_cn: 他将向全班介绍他的朋友。
words.en: If you introduce someone, you tell someone else their name so that they can know each other.

words.ex: He tried to smuggle cigarettes across the border.
words.ex_cn: 他试图走私香烟过境。
words.en: To smuggle goods or people means to move them into or out of a country illegally.

words.tr:
n. 船；舰；
v. 装运；
words.ex: The ship sailed across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船驶过了海洋。
words.en: A ship is a large boat for travelling on water, especially across the sea.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: The inner room is quiet and dark.
words.ex_cn: 内部的房间安静而昏暗。
words.en: Located inside or further in; relating to the mind or spirit.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.tr:
prep. 在（或向）…内；
n. 内部；里面；
adv. 在（或向）里面；
adj. 内部的；里面的；
words.ex: The keys are inside the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: The inside of something is the part that is normally enclosed or hidden by its outer surface.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观是白色的。
words.en: The outer surface or structure of something.

words.tr:
prep. 在...外；
n. 外面；外边；外部；
adv. 在外面；
adj. 外面的；外界的；
words.ex: The cat is sitting outside the house.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在房子外面。
words.en: The outer side or surface of something; not inside a building; external to a particular place or thing.

words.ex: The police found evidence at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了证据。
words.en: Evidence is anything that you see, experience, read, or are told that causes you to believe that something is true or has really happened.

words.ex: The math teacher asked for a proof of the theorem.
words.ex_cn: 数学老师要求给出这个定理的证明。
words.en: Proof is a fact, argument, or piece of evidence which shows that something is definitely true or definitely exists.

words.ex: He proved the theorem with simple math.
words.ex_cn: 他用简单的数学证明了这个定理。
words.en: To prove something means to show that it is true or correct by providing evidence or argument.

words.tr:
adj. 清楚的；明确的；清晰的；清澈的；晴朗的；
v. 清空；清除；放晴；使明确；
adv. 清楚地；彻底地；
words.ex: The instructions are clear.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: Free from anything that marks or darkens; transparent; bright; not obscure or ambiguous; easily understood; free from guilt or blame.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.tr: n. 暗示；提示；有益的建议；
words.ex: He gave me a hint about the surprise party.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我关于惊喜派对的暗示。
words.en: A hint is a slight or indirect indication or suggestion.

words.ex: The teacher gave a cue to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了开始游戏的提示。
words.en: A cue is a signal for someone to do something, or a piece of information that helps someone to understand something.

words.ex: The police found a clue at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了一条线索。
words.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps to solve a problem or mystery.

words.ex: The teacher collected data from the students' tests.
words.ex_cn: 老师收集了学生测试的数据。
words.en: Data is information, especially facts or numbers, collected to be examined and considered and used to help decision-making, or information in an electronic form that can be stored and used by a computer.

words.ex: The teacher gave us important information about the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们关于考试的重要信息。
words.en: Information is facts or details about a subject, event, or situation.

words.ex: The statistics show a rise in sales last year.
words.ex_cn: 这些统计数字显示去年销售额有所上升。
words.en: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data.

words.tr:
adj. 迅速的；敏捷的；快的；
n. 雨燕；
words.ex: The swift runner won the race.
words.ex_cn: 这位迅速的跑步者赢得了比赛。
words.en: moving or capable of moving at great speed, or happening within a very short time; fast.

words.ex: The car moved at a rapid speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车以迅速的速度行驶。
words.en: A rapid change or event happens very quickly.

words.ex: He gave a quick answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对问题给出了一个快速的回答。
words.en: Moving fast or doing something in a short time.

words.ex: He left the room immediately after the bell rang.
words.ex_cn: 铃声一响，他就立即离开了房间。
words.en: If something happens immediately, it happens without any delay.

words.ex: He left the room straightaway after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后他立即离开了房间。
words.en: If you do something straightaway, you do it immediately and without delay.

words.ex: He pressed the button to speed up the video.
words.ex_cn: 他按了按钮来加快视频速度。
words.en: To increase the speed or rate of something.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.tr:
n. 率；速度；比率；价格；费用；
v. 被评价；定级；（被）认为；
words.ex: The interest rate is very low this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年的利率非常低。
words.en: A rate is the speed at which something happens or changes, or the amount or number of something that happens or changes in a particular period.

words.ex: There was a sudden noise in the night.
words.ex_cn: 夜里突然传来一阵响声。
words.en: If something is sudden, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.

words.ex: He drove at a breakneck speed down the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 他以惊险的速度沿着山路开车。
words.en: If you say that something happens or travels at breakneck speed, you mean that it happens or travels very fast.

words.tr: phrase. , n.突然出现：指突然从隐藏的位置迅速出现或活动。; 弹出式：指在打开页面时形成一个立体结构的设备或插图。...
words.ex: A message will pop up when you open the app.
words.ex_cn: 当你打开应用程序时，会弹出一条消息。
words.en: If something such as a message or window pops up on a computer screen, it appears there suddenly.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.ex: The temperature remains high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天温度保持很高。
words.en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.tr:
v. 停留；保持；
n. 停留；逗留；
words.ex: He will stay at home tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚会待在家里。
words.en: To stay means to continue to be in a particular place or situation, or to remain in a specified state or condition.

words.tr:
v. 粘附；（随意）放置；忍受；
n. 棍枝；条状物；球棍；
words.ex: The glue makes the paper stick to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水使纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree. If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.

words.ex: She keeps the room clean every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天保持房间干净。
words.en: To continue to have or hold something; to maintain a condition or position.

words.ex: The company improved data retention after upgrading its system.
words.ex_cn: 公司在升级系统后提高了数据保留能力。
words.en: The action of retaining something; the continued possession, use, or control of something.

words.tr: v. 幸存；生存；存活；艰难挺过；
words.ex: He survived the accident with minor injuries.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中幸存下来，只有轻微受伤。
words.en: If you survive in a dangerous situation, you continue to live or exist in spite of it.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.ex: He suffered from a bad cold last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周患了重感冒。
words.en: To experience something unpleasant, such as injury, pain, or loss.

words.ex: He must face his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: The front part of a person's head from the forehead to the chin, or the corresponding part in an animal.

words.tr:
n. 病人；
adj. 有耐心的；
words.ex: The doctor helped the patient feel better.
words.ex_cn: 医生帮助病人感觉好些了。
words.en: A patient person is able to wait for a long time or deal with a difficult situation without becoming angry or upset.

words.ex: He showed patience while waiting for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他在等公交车时表现出了耐心。
words.en: The ability to stay calm and not get angry, especially when there is a difficulty or you have to wait a long time.

words.ex: He studied hard, thereby passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，因此通过了考试。
words.en: You use thereby to introduce an important result or consequence of the event or action you have just mentioned.

words.ex: It rained all day, therefore the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use therefore to introduce a logical result or conclusion.

words.ex: He was late because the bus was slow.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，因为公交车很慢。
words.en: You use 'because' when stating the reason for something.

words.ex: It rained all day, hence the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use hence to indicate that the statement you are about to make is a consequence of what you have just said.

words.tr:
adv. 如同；和…一样
prep. 作为；如同
conj. 由于；像；当…时；尽管
words.ex: He runs as fast as a cheetah.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得像猎豹一样快。
words.en: used to compare two things, to show that they are similar in some way; used to introduce the reason for something; used to mean 'in the role of'

words.tr:
prep. 自…以后；从…以来；
conj. 因为；由于；既然；从…以后；
adv. 此后；后来；
words.ex: He has lived here since 2020.
words.ex_cn: 他自2020年以来一直住在这里。
words.en: From a past time until now; because; as a result of the fact that.

words.ex: He worked hard, leading to better grades.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，导致成绩提高了。
words.en: Leading to is used to indicate that one thing is a result of another or that one thing causes another.

words.ex: He didn't study hard, as a result, he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有努力学习，结果考试不及格。
words.en: used to introduce the consequence or effect of a particular situation or event

words.ex: He was late because of the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他因为公交车而迟到了。
words.en: You use 'because of' to introduce the reason or explanation for something.

words.ex: Thanks to his help, I passed the test.
words.ex_cn: 多亏了他的帮助，我通过了考试。
words.en: used to say that something good has happened because of someone or something

words.ex: He was late due to traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他因为交通堵塞迟到了。
words.en: If an event is due to something, it happens or exists as a direct result of that thing.

words.ex: He was late owing to the bus delay.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，因为公交车晚点了。
words.en: You use owing to when you are introducing the reason for something.

words.ex: His love of music stems from his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的热爱源于他的童年。
words.en: If a condition or problem stems from something, it was caused originally by that thing.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.tr: 短语. 作为一个促成因素；作为导致某一结果的部分原因
words.ex: Poor diet was as a contributory factor to his illness.
words.ex_cn: 饮食不良是他患病的一个促成因素。
words.en: Acting as one of several factors that contribute to a particular outcome or result.

words.tr:
n. 原因；理由；理性；
v. 推理；推断；
words.ex: The reason for his absence is sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他缺席的原因是生病。
words.en: A reason is an explanation or justification for an action, belief, or occurrence.

words.tr:
v. 导致；引起；
n. 原因；理由；事业；
words.ex: Smoking can cause lung disease.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会导致肺癌。
words.en: The cause of something is what makes it happen or exist.

words.tr:
prep. 为；因为；给；
conj. 因为；由于；
words.ex: I bought this gift for my mother.
words.ex_cn: 我为我妈妈买了这份礼物。
words.en: If something is for a particular person, group, or purpose, it is intended to be used by that person or group or for that purpose.

words.ex: Why did you come late?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么来晚了？
words.en: You use why in questions when you ask about the reasons for something.

words.ex: Can you explain this math problem?
words.ex_cn: 你能解释一下这个数学问题吗？
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by describing or giving information about it.

words.ex: He gave a simple explanation for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的错误给出了一个简单的解释。
words.en: An explanation is a statement or account that makes something clear or provides a reason for something.

words.tr:
n. 帮助；援助；
v. 帮助；协助；
words.ex: The charity provided aid to the flood victims.
words.ex_cn: 慈善机构向洪水受害者提供了帮助。
words.en: To aid someone means to help or assist them. Aid can also refer to the help or support given.

words.tr:
v. 帮助；
n. 帮助；
words.ex: He helps his sister with her homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助妹妹做作业。
words.en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or information.

words.ex: He asked for assistance with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他请求帮助做作业。
words.en: The act of helping or supporting someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 支持；支撑；
n. 拥护；帮助；
words.ex: My friends support me when I feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我感到难过时，我的朋友们支持我。
words.en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

words.tr:
n. 地址；演讲；
v. 解决；向…讲话；
words.ex: Please write your address on the form.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的地址写在表格上。
words.en: The particulars of the place where someone lives or an organization is situated; a formal speech delivered to an audience.

words.ex: The solution to the problem is simple.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的解决办法很简单。
words.en: A solution to a problem is a way of dealing with it so that the difficulty is removed.

words.ex: He solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解决了这道数学题。
words.en: If you solve a problem or a question, you find a solution or an answer to it.

words.ex: He can deal with difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能处理困难的问题。
words.en: To deal with something means to take action in order to achieve something or in order to solve a problem.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.tr:
n. 失败；
v. 击败；战胜；
words.ex: The team accepted the defeat with pride.
words.ex_cn: 球队以自豪的态度接受了失败。
words.en: If you defeat someone, you win a victory over them in a battle, game, or contest.

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.ex: They settled in a small village after retirement.
words.ex_cn: 他们退休后在一个小村庄安顿下来。
words.en: To settle means to resolve or come to an agreement about a dispute, to establish a permanent home in a particular place, or to come to rest in a particular position.

words.ex: He will fix the broken chair tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会修理那把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: To fix something means to repair it, to make it firm or stable, or to arrange or decide it.

words.tr: phrase. 算出；弄明白；解决；想出
words.ex: I can't figure out the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我算不出答案。
words.en: To understand or solve something by thinking about it.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.ex: I managed to finish my homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我设法在晚饭前完成了作业。
words.en: To manage means to be in charge of or control something, especially a business or a group of people.

words.ex: He will tackle the problem tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会处理这个问题。
words.en: If you tackle a problem or task, you deal with it in a determined way. In sports such as football and rugby, a tackle is an act of trying to take the ball from a player on the other team.

words.ex: He tries to cope with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To deal effectively with something difficult.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: The disposal of waste is important for the environment.
words.ex_cn: 废物的处理对环境很重要。
words.en: The act or process of getting rid of something, especially by throwing it away or selling it.

words.ex: The resolution of the conflict took many meetings.
words.ex_cn: 这个冲突的解决花了多次会议。
words.en: A resolution is a formal decision made at a meeting by the vote of the people who are there. It can also refer to a firm decision to do or not to do something.

words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

words.tr:
v. 拙劣地做；搞砸
n. 搞糟了的事情；失误
words.ex: He bungled the simple task.
words.ex_cn: 他把简单的任务搞砸了。
words.en: To bungle something means to do it badly or clumsily, often resulting in failure or mistakes.

words.tr: v. 处理不当；使用不当
words.ex: He mishandled the situation and made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他处理不当，让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you mishandle something, you deal with it badly or carelessly, often causing problems or damage.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: He steers the team toward success.
words.ex_cn: 他引导团队走向成功。
words.en: To steer a vehicle, ship, or aircraft is to control its direction.

words.ex: Good governance helps the city run smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 良好的治理有助于城市顺利运行。
words.en: The way that a country, company, etc. is controlled by the people who run it.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；持有；容纳；保留；举行；
n. 拿；控制；持；
words.ex: He held the rope tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; to maintain in a grasp; to keep in a specified state, relation, or position; to contain or be capable of containing; to have in one's possession; to keep back from action; to delay the action or effect of; to keep in custody; to bear, sustain, or support; to have or maintain in the mind; to consider or esteem; to assert or affirm; to organize and carry on; to have the ownership or use of; to keep from falling or moving; to remain unbroken or unyielding; to remain attached or faithful; to remain valid or effective.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.tr:
n. 控制；管制；
v. 控制；操纵；
words.ex: The teacher has good control of the class.
words.ex_cn: 老师对课堂有很好的控制。
words.en: To control something means to have power over it and to be able to make it do what you want.

words.tr:
n. 规则；统治；
v. 统治；
words.ex: The teacher made a new rule for homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师制定了一个新的作业规则。
words.en: A rule is a statement telling people what they should do in order to achieve success or a benefit of some kind.

words.ex: The thermostat helps regulate the room temperature.
words.ex_cn: 恒温器有助于调节室温。
words.en: To regulate something means to control or manage it, especially by means of rules or laws.

words.tr:
v. 引导；领导；带头；
n. 主导地位；铅；领先；
words.ex: The teacher leads the students to the library.
words.ex_cn: 老师带领学生去图书馆。
words.en: To be in charge of a group, country, or situation; to guide or direct in a course; a position of advantage in a contest or competition; a heavy, malleable, ductile, bluish-white, dense metallic element.

words.tr:
n. 影响（力）；
v. 影响；
words.ex: The teacher had a big influence on her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生们有很大的影响。
words.en: The power to affect, control, or manipulate someone or something.

words.ex: He will take over the business next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将接管这家企业。
words.en: To take control of something, especially a company, by buying a majority of its shares or by getting a position of power within it.

words.tr:
n. 力量；电源；权力；强国；
v. 给…提供能量；供以动力；
words.ex: The power of the storm broke the trees.
words.ex_cn: 风暴的力量折断了树木。
words.en: The ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way; control or influence over others; electrical energy supplied to a device or building.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.ex: He showed strong emotion when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，表现出了强烈的情绪。
words.en: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

words.tr: n. 感觉； v. 感到；“feel”的现在分词；
words.ex: I have a feeling it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我感觉明天会下雨。
words.en: An emotion or a physical sensation.

words.tr:
n. 意义；感知；理解力；知觉；
v. 感觉到；觉察出；意识到；
words.ex: The story has no sense.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事没有意义。
words.en: A sense is a feeling or awareness about something, or a physical ability such as sight, hearing, touch, taste, or smell.

words.ex: His mood changed after he heard the good news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个好消息后，心情变了。
words.en: A mood is a temporary state of mind or feeling.

words.ex: Children develop perceptual skills by playing with toys.
words.ex_cn: 儿童通过玩玩具发展知觉能力。
words.en: Relating to the ability to interpret or become aware of something through the senses.

words.tr:
n. 婴儿；
adj. 初期的；
words.ex: The infant is sleeping in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在婴儿床里睡觉。
words.en: An infant is a baby or very young child.

words.ex: The baby is sleeping in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在婴儿床里睡觉。
words.en: A baby is a very young child, especially one that cannot yet walk or talk.

words.ex: The child is playing with toys.
words.ex_cn: 这个儿童正在玩玩具。
words.en: A child is a human being who is not yet an adult.

words.tr:
n. 小孩；
v. 开玩笑；
words.ex: The kid is playing with a ball.
words.ex_cn: 小孩在玩球。
words.en: A kid is a child or young person. As a verb, to kid means to tease or deceive someone in a playful way.

words.ex: The children are playing in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在公园里玩耍。
words.en: Children are people who are not yet adults, typically those who are under the age of 18.

words.ex: The young boy plays soccer every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻的孩子每天下午都踢足球。
words.en: Someone who is young has not lived for very long or is not yet mature.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.ex: He remembers his childhood as a happy time.
words.ex_cn: 他记得自己的童年是一段快乐的时光。
words.en: Childhood is the period of a person's life when they are a child.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: The construction of the new bridge took two years.
words.ex_cn: 新桥的建筑花了两年时间。
words.en: The process or method of building or making something, especially buildings, bridges, etc.

words.tr: n. 建筑物；楼房； v. 建筑；“build”的现在分词；
words.ex: The tall building has 20 floors.
words.ex_cn: 这栋高楼有20层。
words.en: A building is a structure that has a roof and walls and stands more or less permanently in one place.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.tr:
v. 建筑；建造；逐步加强；
n. 体格；体形；
words.ex: They build a house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他们在湖边建了一所房子。
words.en: To construct something by putting parts or material together.

words.tr: v. 使得；制作；做；“make”的现在分词； n. 制造；
words.ex: The rain is making the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使得道路变得滑。
words.en: The process of creating or producing something.

words.tr: v. 构造； n. v. 构造（construct 的现在分词）；
words.ex: He is constructing a model house with blocks.
words.ex_cn: 他正在用积木搭建一个模型房子。
words.en: The act of building or creating something, especially a large structure or system.

words.ex: The framework of the house is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 房子的骨架是木制的。
words.en: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

words.ex: The old estate has large gardens and a beautiful mansion.
words.ex_cn: 这个古老的庄园有大片花园和一座美丽的豪宅。
words.en: An estate is all the money and property that someone owns, especially everything that is left when they die.

words.ex: He lost all his property in the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他在火灾中失去了所有财产。
words.en: Something owned; a possession.

words.ex: He works in real estate in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约从事房地产行业。
words.en: Real estate refers to property consisting of land or buildings.

words.tr:
n. 风险；
v. 冒...的危险；
words.ex: He took a risk by starting his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他创业时承担了风险。
words.en: If there is a risk of something unpleasant, there is a possibility that it will happen.

words.ex: The country is facing an economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正面临经济危机。
words.en: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

words.ex: There is danger near the river.
words.ex_cn: 河边有危险。
words.en: Danger is the possibility that someone may be harmed or killed.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.ex: Smoking can jeopardise your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put something such as a plan or system in danger of being harmed or damaged.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.ex: The storm is a threat to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对村庄构成了威胁。
words.en: A threat is a statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage, or other hostile action on someone in retribution for something done or not done.

words.tr: n. 掠夺者；捕食性动物；食肉动物；
words.ex: The lion is a predator that hunts deer.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种捕食鹿的掠夺者。
words.en: A predator is an animal that naturally preys on others.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.ex: The hostile neighbor shouted at us every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个敌意的邻居每天早上都对我们大喊大叫。
words.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behavior.

words.ex: The soldier fought against his enemy in the war.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在战争中与他的敌人作战。
words.en: An enemy is someone who opposes you, competes with you, or is hostile towards you.

words.ex: He saw his neighbor as a foe.
words.ex_cn: 他把邻居看作敌人。
words.en: A foe is someone who opposes or fights against another; an enemy.

words.ex: The location of the store is near the park.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的位置在公园附近。
words.en: A location is the place where something happens or is situated.

words.tr: n. 位置；职位；地位；姿势；
words.ex: The book is on the table in a good position.
words.ex_cn: 书放在桌子上的一个好位置。
words.en: A position refers to the place or type of role someone has in a situation, organization, or society, or the way in which someone or something is placed or arranged.

words.tr:
n. 地点；场所；斑点；
v. 发现；识别；
words.ex: This is the spot where we met for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
words.en: A spot is a particular place or point. It can also refer to a small mark or stain, or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to see, notice, or recognize someone or something.

words.ex: The site of the old church is now a park.
words.ex_cn: 旧教堂的位置现在是一个公园。
words.en: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens.

words.tr:
n. 地方；方位；
v. 安放；安置；
words.ex: This is a quiet place to read books.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个安静的地方读书。
words.en: A particular position or point in space.

words.ex: Where is the book?
words.ex_cn: 书在哪里？
words.en: You use where to ask questions about the place or position of someone or something, or to indicate the place or position of someone or something.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.ex: The lawyer helps people with legal problems.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助人们解决法律问题。
words.en: A lawyer is a person who is qualified to advise people about the law and represent them in court.

words.ex: He hired a solicitor to help with his house sale.
words.ex_cn: 他聘请了一名事务律师来帮助处理他的房屋出售。
words.en: A solicitor is a lawyer who gives legal advice and prepares legal documents, especially in England.

words.ex: He broke the law and was arrested.
words.ex_cn: 他违反了法律，被逮捕了。
words.en: A law is a rule or set of rules for good behaviour which is considered right and important by the majority of people for moral, religious, or emotional reasons.

words.tr:
v. 行动；表现；演戏；
n. 行动；法令；
words.ex: He acted quickly to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速行动救了那个孩子。
words.en: To do something for a particular purpose or in a particular way; to behave in a particular way; to have an effect or influence on something; to perform a part in a play, film, etc.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: The government made a new regulation to control pollution.
words.ex_cn: 政府出台了一项新管理措施来控制污染。
words.en: A regulation is an official rule or order.

words.ex: He always follows the principle of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循诚实的原则。
words.en: A principle is a basic idea or rule that explains or controls how something happens or works.

words.ex: Follow the guideline to complete the form.
words.ex_cn: 按照指导路线完成表格。
words.en: A guideline is a set of rules or instructions that are given by an official organization telling you how to do something, especially something difficult.

words.ex: The teacher gave clear instruction on how to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了如何解决这个问题的明确教授。
words.en: Detailed information telling how something should be done, operated, or assembled.

words.ex: The government changed its education policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府改变了它的教育政策。
words.en: A policy is a set of ideas or plans that is used as a basis for making decisions, especially in politics, economics, or business.

words.ex: The norm in this school is to arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的准则就是准时到校。
words.en: A norm is an official standard or level that organizations are expected to reach.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.tr: n. 进展；进步；缓慢前进；稳步前进；
words.ex: The project shows slow progress.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目进展缓慢。
words.en: Progress is the process of gradually improving or getting nearer to achieving or completing something.

words.tr:
v. 大步行走；跨一大步
n. 大步；步伐
words.ex: He takes a long stride when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时迈着大步。
words.en: To walk with long, decisive steps in a specified direction.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；
v. 分阶段进行；
words.ex: The project is in its final phase.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正处于最后阶段。
words.en: A phase is a particular stage in a process or in the gradual development of something.

words.ex: Follow the procedure step by step.
words.ex_cn: 一步一步地按照步骤进行。
words.en: A procedure is a way of doing something, especially the usual or correct way.

words.tr:
n. 方法；接近；靠近；路径；
v. 接近；靠近；临近；处理；
words.ex: He used a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一种新方法来解决问题。
words.en: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time.

words.tr: n. 方式；道路；方向；路线；方法；
words.ex: He found a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一种解决这个问题的新方式。
words.en: A way is a method, style, or manner of doing something, or a route or path that you take to get from one place to another.

words.ex: He found a new method to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: A method is a particular way of doing something.

words.tr:
n. 练习；实践；惯常做法；
v. 从事；练习；
words.ex: Daily practice helps you improve your skills.
words.ex_cn: 每天的练习帮助你提高技能。
words.en: Practice is the act of rehearsing a behavior over and over, or engaging in an activity again and again, for the purpose of improving or mastering it, as in the phrase 'practice makes perfect'.

words.tr:
n. 锻炼；行使；练习；
v. 运用；使用；锻炼；
words.ex: He does exercise every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上锻炼以保持健康。
words.en: Physical activity that you do to make your body strong and healthy.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；大量的；辽阔的；
words.ex: The desert is vast and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠巨大而空旷。
words.en: If you describe something as vast, you mean that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: He has a large house.
words.ex_cn: 他有一所大房子。
words.en: Something that is large is greater in size than usual or average.

words.ex: He is a big boy now.
words.ex_cn: 他现在是个大男孩了。
words.en: Of considerable size or extent; larger than other items of its kind.

words.ex: The dog is huge.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很大。
words.en: Extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: He showed the utmost care when handling the fragile glass.
words.ex_cn: 他在处理易碎的玻璃时表现出了最大的小心。
words.en: The greatest or highest degree of something.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.ex: He has a small dog.
words.ex_cn: 他有一只小狗。
words.en: If something is small, it is not large in size or amount.

words.ex: There is little water left in the bottle.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里剩下的水很少。
words.en: Small in size, amount, or degree (often used to convey an appealing diminutiveness or express an affectionate or dismissive attitude).

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.tr: adj. 极小的；微小的；微量的；
words.ex: The tiny ant carried a big leaf.
words.ex_cn: 这只极小的蚂蚁搬着一片大叶子。
words.en: Very small in size or amount.

words.tr: adj. 有限的； v. 限制；“limit”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: We have limited time to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 我们完成这个项目的时间是有限的。
words.en: If something is limited, there is only a certain amount of it.

words.tr: v. 缺乏；“lack”的现在分词； adj. 缺乏的；
words.ex: He is lacking confidence in speaking English.
words.ex_cn: 他在说英语时缺乏信心。
words.en: If something is lacking, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

words.ex: His deficiency in math made him struggle in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的缺乏让他在课堂上很吃力。
words.en: A deficiency is a lack or shortage of something that is needed.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.tr: adv. 较少地；更少地；“little”的比较级； adj. 更少的；“little”的比较级； pron. 较少；更少；
words.ex: He eats less sugar now.
words.ex_cn: 他现在吃得更少的糖。
words.en: You use less to indicate that there is a smaller amount of something than before or than average. You can use 'less' to indicate that something is smaller in size or degree than another thing.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimise waste in your daily life.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少日常生活中的浪费。
words.en: If you minimise a risk, problem, or unpleasant situation, you reduce it to the lowest possible level, or prevent it increasing beyond that level.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.tr:
n. 最小值；
adj. 最小量的；
words.ex: The minimum of the function is 5.
words.ex_cn: 这个函数的最小值是5。
words.en: The minimum is the smallest or least amount possible or allowed.

words.ex: His absence of interest made the teacher sad.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习的缺乏兴趣让老师感到难过。
words.en: The state of being away from a place or person.

words.ex: He has a considerable amount of money.
words.ex_cn: 他有相当多的钱。
words.en: Considerable means large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: There is plenty of food on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌上有很多食物。
words.en: A large quantity or number; more than enough.

words.tr:
adj. 许多的；
pron. 许多人或物；
words.ex: Many students like to play soccer after school.
words.ex_cn: 许多学生喜欢放学后踢足球。
words.en: A large number of.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

words.ex: A number of students are late for class.
words.ex_cn: 许多学生上课迟到了。
words.en: An indefinite but considerable amount or quantity of something.

words.tr: adj. 无数的；多的；数不清的；
words.ex: There are countless stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数颗星星。
words.en: Too numerous to count.

words.ex: He has a lot of books.
words.ex_cn: 他有很多书。
words.en: A large number or amount of something.

words.ex: There are lots of books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: A large number or amount of something.

words.tr:
pron. 几个；一些；
adj. 不同的；
words.ex: I have several books on the table.
words.ex_cn: 我桌上放着几本书。
words.en: Several means a number of people or things that is more than a few but not a lot.

words.ex: I have a few apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 我桌上有一些苹果。
words.en: A small number of things or people.

words.tr:
adj. 一些；某些；
pron. 有些；若干；
words.ex: I need some water.
words.ex_cn: 我需要一些水。
words.en: used to refer to an unspecified amount or number of something

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；不同的；各种的；
words.ex: He bought various fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you say that there are various things, you mean there are several different things of the type mentioned.

words.ex: The store offers multiple flavors of ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供多种口味的冰淇淋。
words.en: If something is multiple, it consists of or involves many things of the same kind.

words.tr:
adj. 大规模的；大量的；
n. 大量；质量；块；群；团；
words.ex: The company launched a mass production line to meet demand.
words.ex_cn: 该公司启动了大规模生产线以满足需求。
words.en: A mass is a large amount of something that has no particular shape or arrangement.

words.ex: He bought a quantity of apples at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一定量的苹果。
words.en: The amount or number of something, especially in relation to measurement or count.

words.ex: The quantity of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: A quantity is an amount that you can measure or count.

words.ex: The quality of this phone is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的质量很高。
words.en: The standard of something as measured against other things of a similar kind; the degree of excellence of something.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.tr: adj. 更高的；高等级的；“high”的比较级； adv. 在更高处；“high”的比较级；
words.ex: He got a higher score than his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他比他的朋友得分更高。
words.en: Higher is the comparative form of 'high', meaning at or to a greater level or degree.

words.ex: The upper shelf is too high to reach.
words.ex_cn: 上面的架子太高了，够不着。
words.en: Higher in place or position; situated above another part.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的；一流的；处于领导地位的； v. “lead”的现在分词；带领；领导；
words.ex: He is the leading scientist in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的科学家。
words.en: If something is leading in a particular area, it is the most important or advanced thing in that area.

words.tr: phrase. 刀刃；尖端；最前沿；优势
words.ex: The knife has a sharp cutting edge.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀有一个锋利的刀刃。
words.en: The most advanced stage in the development of something; the forefront.

words.tr: adj. 先进的；高级的； v. 提前；前进；“advance”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This school uses advanced technology in classrooms.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校在教室里使用先进的技术。
words.en: An advanced system, method, or design is modern and has been developed from an earlier version of the same thing.

words.tr:
adv. 更加；
adj. 更多的；
pron. 更多的人或物；
words.ex: She wants to learn more about science.
words.ex_cn: 她想更深入了解科学。
words.en: You use 'more' to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else. You can use 'more' with a noun to indicate that there is a greater amount of it than before or than average, or than something else.

words.tr: phrase. 前缘；重要位置；前沿
words.ex: The plane's leading edge is designed to reduce air resistance.
words.ex_cn: 飞机的前缘设计用于减少空气阻力。
words.en: The most advanced position in a particular field or activity.

words.tr: adj. 更好的；更优秀的；“good”的比较级； adv. 更好地；“well”的比较级； v. 胜过；使更佳；
words.ex: This shirt is better than the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫比那件更好。
words.en: If something is better, it is of a higher standard, quality, or level than something else, or than it was before.

words.ex: This job requires patience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作需要耐心。
words.en: If you require something, you need it or want it.

words.ex: I want a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

words.tr:
n. 需求；要求；
v. 要求；需求；
words.ex: The demand for clean water is increasing.
words.ex_cn: 对清洁水的需求正在增加。
words.en: If you demand something, you ask for it very forcefully, often because you think you have a right to do so.

words.tr:
v. 需要；
n. 需要；
words.ex: I need help with my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我需要帮助做作业。
words.en: If you need something, you must have it because it is essential.

words.tr: phrase. 呼吁；号召；要求；接（人）
words.ex: The situation calls for immediate action.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要立即采取行动。
words.en: If you call for something, you demand that it should happen.

words.ex: He asks for help when he is stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当他遇到困难时，他会寻求帮助。
words.en: To request something; to express a desire for something.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；必要的；必然的；
words.ex: Water is necessary for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命所必需的。
words.en: If something is necessary, it is needed in order for something else to happen or be done.

words.ex: He protects the environment by recycling.
words.ex_cn: 他通过回收利用来保护环境。
words.en: The environment is the natural world in which people, animals, and plants live.

words.tr: adj. 周围的； v. “surround”的现在分词；
words.ex: The surrounding trees block the wind.
words.ex_cn: 周围的树木挡住了风。
words.en: The area or environment around something or someone.

words.tr: v. 设置；放；“set”的现在分词； n. 环境；背景；
words.ex: He is setting the alarm for 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把闹钟设置为早上6点。
words.en: The context and environment in which something is set or takes place.

words.ex: He changed his job because of his background.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的背景换了工作。
words.en: The background is the situation that exists at a particular time, or the situation in which something happens, which helps to explain it.

words.ex: Under these circumstances, we had to cancel the trip.
words.ex_cn: 在这种情况下，我们不得不取消旅行。
words.en: A circumstance is a fact or event that makes a situation the way it is.

words.ex: The atmosphere keeps the Earth warm.
words.ex_cn: 大气使地球保持温暖。
words.en: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding a planet or other material body, held in place by the gravity of the body.

words.ex: The situation is very serious.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况非常严重。
words.en: A situation is all the circumstances and things that are happening at a particular time and in a particular place.

words.ex: His condition improved after the treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他的状况在接受治疗后好转了。
words.en: A condition is a state of affairs that must exist or be brought about before something else can happen or be done.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.ex: The weather is sunny today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气晴朗。
words.en: The condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, especially with regard to temperature, precipitation, and wind.

words.ex: The climate in summer is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 夏天的气候非常炎热。
words.en: The climate of a place is the general weather conditions that are typical of it.

words.ex: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
words.ex_cn: 植物从空气中吸收二氧化碳。
words.en: Carbon dioxide is a gas that is produced when people and animals breathe out, or when carbon is burned in the air. It is used by plants in photosynthesis.

words.ex: Global warming is making the Earth hotter.
words.ex_cn: 全球变暖正在让地球变得更热。
words.en: Global warming refers to the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily fossil fuel burning, which increases heat-trapping greenhouse gas levels in Earth's atmosphere.

words.ex: Climate change is making the weather hotter.
words.ex_cn: 气候变化让天气变得更热。
words.en: A significant and lasting change in the Earth's climate, especially a change due to an increase in the average atmospheric temperature.

words.tr: adj. 对生态环境友好的；不妨害生态环境的
words.ex: She uses eco-friendly bags to shop.
words.ex_cn: 她购物时使用环保袋。
words.en: Eco-friendly refers to goods, services, laws, and guidelines that claim reduced, minimal, or no harm upon ecosystems or the environment.

words.tr: n. 保护；节约（自然资源）；
words.ex: The park is for the conservation of wild animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是为了保护野生动物。
words.en: The protection and preservation of the natural environment and wildlife.

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.ex: Farmers grow tomatoes in a greenhouse.
words.ex_cn: 农民在温室里种植番茄。
words.en: A greenhouse is a building with glass walls and roof; for the cultivation and exhibition of plants under controlled conditions.

words.ex: The planet Mars is red.
words.ex_cn: 火星是红色的。
words.en: A planet is a large object in space that moves around a star, such as the sun, and does not produce its own light.

words.ex: The factory releases a pollutant into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向河里排放一种污染物。
words.en: A pollutant is a substance that pollutes something, especially air, water, or soil.

words.ex: The river is dirty because of pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这条河因为污染而变得肮脏。
words.en: Pollution is the process of making air, water, soil, etc. dirty and not safe or suitable to use.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: The river suffered from contamination after the factory dumped waste.
words.ex_cn: 工厂倾倒废物后，这条河受到了污染。
words.en: The process of making something dirty or polluted, or the state of being dirty or polluted.

words.tr: phrase. 烟与烟雾；常指工业排放的废气或令人不悦的气味
words.ex: The factory releases smoke and fume into the air.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向空气中排放烟雾和废气。
words.en: Smoke and fume refer to the visible gaseous products of combustion or other chemical reactions, often considered pollutants.

words.ex: He burns coal to keep his house warm.
words.ex_cn: 他烧煤来让房子暖和。
words.en: Coal is a hard black substance that is extracted from the ground and burned as fuel.

words.ex: He drew a picture with charcoal.
words.ex_cn: 他用木炭画了一幅画。
words.en: Charcoal is a black substance made by burning wood slowly in an oven with little air, used for drawing or as a fuel.

words.tr:
n. 燃料；燃油；
v. 加剧；
words.ex: The rocket uses fuel 627 for propulsion.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用627号燃料推进。
words.en: Fuel is a substance such as coal, gas, or oil that is burned to provide heat or power.

words.ex: He collected firewood for the campfire.
words.ex_cn: 他为篝火收集了木柴。
words.en: Wood that is cut and used for fuel in fires.

words.ex: We need sustainable energy to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要可持续的能源来保护环境。
words.en: If something is sustainable, it can be maintained or continued at a certain rate or level without causing damage or depletion of resources.

words.ex: He saves money for long-term goals.
words.ex_cn: 他为长期目标存钱。
words.en: Something that is long-term has continued for a long time or will continue for a long time in the future.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: My family follows the tradition of eating dumplings on New Year's Eve.
words.ex_cn: 我的家庭遵循除夕吃饺子的传统。
words.en: A tradition is a custom or belief that has existed for a long time among a particular group of people.

words.tr:
adj. 典范的；典型的；
n. 文学经典；名著；优秀的典范；
words.ex: This movie is a classic comedy.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部典范的喜剧。
words.en: A classic is something that is judged to be of the highest quality and outstanding of its kind.

words.tr: adv. 早些时候；“early”的比较级； adj. 之前的；早期的；“early”的比较级；
words.ex: He left the party earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他早些时候离开了派对。
words.en: Before the present time or before the time one is referring to.

words.ex: He wears traditional clothes on holidays.
words.ex_cn: 他在节日时穿传统服装。
words.en: Traditional refers to customs, beliefs, or methods that have existed for a long time without changing.

words.ex: He listens to classical music every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上听古典音乐。
words.en: Classical refers to music, literature, or art that is considered to be of the highest quality and of lasting value, especially from the ancient Greek or Roman periods or from the 18th and early 19th centuries.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.ex: The virus made many people sick.
words.ex_cn: 这个病毒让很多人病了。
words.en: A virus is a very small organism that causes infectious diseases in people, animals, and plants.

words.ex: Washing hands can kill germs.
words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: Bacteria can make you sick.
words.ex_cn: 细菌会让你生病。
words.en: Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause diseases.

words.tr: n. 霉菌；菌类；真菌；“fungus”的复数；
words.ex: The bread has fungi growing on it.
words.ex_cn: 面包上长了霉菌。
words.en: Fungi are a group of living organisms which are classified in their own kingdom. This means they are not animals, plants, or bacteria. Fungi include mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.

words.ex: He works in a medical center.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家医疗中心工作。
words.en: Relating to the science or practice of medicine.

words.ex: Good food and sleep help maintain health.
words.ex_cn: 良好的饮食和睡眠有助于保持健康。
words.en: The condition of a person's body or mind, especially in terms of the presence or absence of illnesses, injuries, or impairments.

words.ex: Exercise helps with your well-being.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有助于你的健康。
words.en: The state of being comfortable, healthy, or happy.
